scope: The Cartesian product of 55 item names previously witnessed by seeded replay and all 40 legal fourth-move/empty-slot candidates at one fixed Zapdos/Marowak decision. Every one of 2200 teams passes native validation and reproduces all 33 public-history boundaries with the original seed and semantic choices. Stats, happiness and counter state stay fixed. This is not a complete information set: previous failures with this seed do not exclude other chance histories, and stat combinations are not covered. The first-action mix is fixed from the earlier 43-world analysis and is not retuned on this product. It uses a common Rock Slide continuation. Each two-step lower witness faces all replies; truncated mass remains [0,1]. An omitted Rock Slide witness uses the universal lower bound zero only when the Sword Dance contribution alone suffices. Rational backups and every policy action are checked. Seven boundary/control/heaviest worlds are replayed, with matching full certificates. The dual upper certificate reuses the two immutable item-world ledgers and their precommitted opponent policy, revalidated against generated model keys. Engine transitions and guarded-state identity remain trusted. The output is an offline proof of a restricted robust game, not an online runtime, full-game ceiling, human calibration or deployed-bot improvement.
